Subject: Telemetry pricing for expanded PoC

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the trace-level charts and the prefix-caching example sold our infra team. We're moving from a 2-week PoC to a month-long evaluation across two product squads, and procurement asked me to get a clearer picture of add-on pricing: specifically retention tiers for tracing, per-dashboard seat pricing for the advanced dashboards, and how credits are applied when we commit to a monthly token/ingest commitment.

High-level ask: can you share an example price path (commit level -> retention window -> dashboard seats -> effective credits/discount) and any flexible ramp options? We expect bursty volume (peak during launches) but want a predictable monthly charge.

Attaching a short usage snapshot we produced.

Hi Liam — great to hear the demo resonated. Short answer: yes, we can do a tiered retention + seat bundle with a stepped discount as you commit more and can offer a pilot credit for the month-long expanded evaluation.

I've put together a concise SOW and a pricing workbook that lays out three paths:
- Pay-as-you-go (no commit) — per-GB ingest, per-GB retained-month, per-dashboard-seat
- Committed monthly credits (tokens/ingest) with retention buckets (30/90/365 days) and seat discounts by band
- Hybrid (commit + overage pricing) — best for bursty workloads

I'll send the SOW + workbook attached. For the initial conversation, would you be open to a short call Thursday to walk through the numbers and a sample credit allocation tied to your projected usage? If procurement wants contract language up front, I can pull in legal.

Best,

From: ben_carter@redwood.com

Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Tracedata pricing approach

Olga/Marissa — quick internal note before we hop on the call. A few constraints and suggestions:

1) Pilot credit: we typically offer a one-month $10k consumption credit for PoC expansions; if they convert to a 12-month reserved capacity/commit, we can apply that credit to the first invoice.

2) Seats vs. usage: prefer to frame advanced dashboards as "seat licenses + visualization compute". Seat discounts kick in at 25/50 seats, but we can make an exception for a 12-month commit (15% off seats at 15 seats).

3) Retention buckets: standard pricing is 30/90/365; offer a 10% discount on 90-day when combined with a commit >= $75k/mo equivalent. For 365-day retention, require a >$200k ARR committed path (or equivalent credits), but for strategic logos we can carve a 6-month ramp.

4) Attachments: make sure the workbook shows an "example effective unit price" row — procurement likes that.

If legal is needed for non-standard concession (seat cliff at 15 instead of 25), I'll flag this early.

— Ben

From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@tracedata.io>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, Ashley Park <ashley.park@acme-corp.com>, procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 11:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Telemetry pricing for expanded PoC

Hi Liam, Ashley — following up with the concrete options we discussed internally. Summary below and attached workbook shows the math. Happy to run the numbers live on our call.

Option A — No commit (fastest):
- 30-day retention by default; advanced dashboards: $35/seat/month; tracing storage $0.045/GB/month
- Good for short PoC, but unit economics higher during sustained use

Option B — Month-to-month commit (recommended for your expanded PoC):
- Commit $30k/month credits for ingest/compute; get 90-day retention at effective -10% on retention unit price
- Dashboard seats: $30/seat/month with a 10% seat credit applied as early-conversion incentive
- We include a one-month $10k pilot credit applied immediately (refundable against first committed invoice)

Option C — 12-month reserved path (preferred for predictable cost):
- Commit $90k/month or equivalent usage credits -> 365-day retention by default, dashboard seats at $25/seat/month, additional 15% volume discount on retention storage
- Dedicated SLA and priority support included

Call to action: can we do Thursday 5/14 at 2pm PT for a 30-minute walk-through? If procurement wants draft terms, I can attach a redlineable clause.

Thanks,
Olga

Ashley/Liam/Team — thanks for the clarity. Per your procurement checklist, attached is a 3-month ramp scenario in the workbook and a short export policy excerpt. Highlights:

- Example ramp: month 1 = 40% peak -> $13.2k after pilot credit; month 2 = 70% -> $21.8k; month 3 = 100% -> $31.0k (numbers assume Option B $30k commit baseline; workbook has full breakdown)
- Seat flexibility: we can grant the 15-seat discount level for a 12-month committed path even though standard cliff is 25 seats. We'll show the adjusted seat-line in the SOW.
- Data export: standard export is compressed JSON/Parquet, included as one-time export at no additional cost for commitments >= 6 months; for month-to-month customers there's a $500 admin fee per export.
